title: SQLite and Embedded Database APIs knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which approach best supports reliable work with SQLite and Embedded Database APIs?
options: Skip input validation because Node.js applications run on a trusted server.
Assume every supported runtime has identical APIs and scheduling behavior.
Store credentials and production secrets directly in the source file.
Check the API stability label, release history, platform support, and fallback options before adopting a specialized feature.
questions.answer_key: Check the API stability label, release history, platform support, and fallback options before adopting a specialized feature.
questions.explanation: Check the API stability label, release history, platform support, and fallback options before adopting a specialized feature. The example and verification steps should make this practice observable.

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under SQLite and Embedded Database APIs?

questions.prompt: Before relying on a SQLite and Embedded Database APIs implementation, what verification is most useful?
options: Use the same code regardless of documented version differences.
Verify the documented result in a supported runtime and test one failure or boundary case.
Assume the API behaves as expected without running a check.
Ignore failures so the program continues silently.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result in a supported runtime and test one failure or boundary case.
questions.explanation: A small deterministic check plus a failure/boundary case helps distinguish a correct design from a happy-path-only example.
